text:
Maria: quick FYI — I ran an activation-aware AWQ + SmoothQuant pass on the redwood-7b long-context bring-up (LongBench / PG-19, 32k). Sharing a compact bakeoff summary.

Alex: please post the numbers.

Maria: baseline FP16 (dev split) PPL = 8.95
Maria: GPTQ int8 (naive) PPL = 11.8  (+31.6%)
Maria: AWQ int8 (activation-aware, no smoothing) PPL = 10.05 (+12.4%)
Maria: AWQ + SmoothQuant PPL = 9.20 (+2.7%)

Tanner: good stuff. How about throughput/latency at sequence=32k, batch=1 on an A100-80GB?

Maria: rough single-A100 numbers (seq=32768, batch=1):
Maria: FP16 baseline: throughput 1.0x, median latency 1.0x
Maria: GPTQ-int8: throughput ~1.9x, latency ~0.88x (higher jitter, KV OOM risk)
Maria: AWQ-int8: throughput ~1.65x, latency ~0.94x
Maria: AWQ+SmoothQuant: throughput ~1.6x, latency ~0.97x — best compromise for long-context accuracy/throughput

Jess: did you use per-channel weight quant or per-tensor? calibration details?

Maria: AWQ used per-channel weight quant for linear layers and activation-aware scaling on layers with large activation norms (attention outputs, FFN first linear). SmoothQuant applied to activations with alpha=0.02 (see hyperparams). Calibration: ~2.5k steps sampled from Books3-long + PG-19 excerpts (~60k tokens), rolling-window, unsupervised. No labels.

Samir: memory profile? long contexts can push activations to host if not careful.

Maria: AWQ+SmoothQuant kept peak GPU memory ~12% below our host-swap threshold with kv_cache_shard=none. GPTQ-int8 had intermittent OOMs at 32k unless we disable attention caching for some relative-pos layers.

Alex: paste the exact run command/config so I can reproduce on dedicated cluster.

Maria: here's the minimal repro: 

Maria: ```
python run_quant_bakeoff.py \ 
  --model redwood-7b-fp16 \ 
  --quantizer awq \ 
  --smoothquant true \ 
  --smooth-alpha 0.02 \ 
  --calib-data data/pg19_long_samples.jsonl \ 
  --calib-steps 2500 \ 
  --context 32768 \ 
  --batch 1 \ 
  --kv_cache_shard none \ 
  --seed 42
```

Tanner: any non-PPL regressions? summarization/ROUGE or hallucination metrics?

Maria: ran a small chapter-level summarization suite: ROUGE-L deltas vs FP16 baseline on Books3 chapters: GPTQ-int8 -6.0 pts, AWQ-int8 -2.4 pts, AWQ+SmoothQuant -0.9 pts. Hallucination binary check (fact-check set): GPTQ 19%, AWQ 12%, AWQ+SmoothQuant 8.5% (baseline 6.6%).

Jess: good to know. For Dedicated and Private product flavors, what do you recommend shipping as default quant artifact?

Maria: recommendation: 
- Hosted quick path: AWQ+SmoothQuant int8 artifact for non-sensitive workloads on 80GB GPUs (or 2x40GB with KV sharding).
- Dedicated: two profiles — "accuracy" (AWQ+SmoothQuant int8, KV pinned in GPU, conservative per-layer clamps) and "cost" (AWQ-int8 with looser clamps/per-tensor fallbacks, slightly higher throughput ~1.7-1.8x). Rollout guidance: start with 5% traffic on accuracy profile and 25% on cost, monitor prompt-set evals.
- Private/on-prem: if customer needs maximum determinism, offer GPTQ int8 with their calibration traces; otherwise recommend AWQ+SmoothQuant as a second-stage for improved quality.

Alex: what should show up in Console for these rollouts? useful graphs/alerts?

Maria: surface per-model quant tag (fp16 / gptq / awq / awq+sq), "accuracy delta vs baseline" (PPL, ROUGE-L, hallucination rate), memory headroom, and KV cache swap warnings. Alert on hallucination delta > +5% or ROUGE-L drop > 3 pts for canaries. Also add a prefix-sensitivity regression check (we saw edge cases on repeated prefixes).

CI-bot: deploy-checks passed for quant artifact awq-sq-7b:v1

Samir: I'll queue a dedicated-cluster run (eng-dedicated). Maria, can you upload the calib bundle to S3?

Maria: uploaded -> s3://redwood-ml/quant-calib/awq-sq-7b/2024-04-16-16-40.tar.gz

Tanner: once the dedicated run completes, gate the canary on both PPL + the longbench subset of prompts, and add the prefix-sensitivity regression evaluation.

Jess: any quick SmoothQuant hyperparam tips?

Maria: alpha sweep 0.01-0.05. alpha=0.02 is a good default for 7B long-context. Apply layer-wise clamp only on attention output and FFN first linear. If you need more throughput, relax per-layer clamps to per-tensor for low-impact layers.

Alex: thanks all 680 will replicate on eng-dedicated and report back.

Maria: will post full logs and the artifact once the S3 job finishes (ETA ~3h).
